articles.title: Movies, Games, Editing: It All Happens on the Lenovo Legion 5i Laptop's Display
articles.summary: Media viewing is becoming more of a one-on-one experience: one person, one monitor. Long gone are the days of a family competing over a television in the living room. Watching movies, playing video games, browsing the internet, doing homework, and a multitude of other visual tasks are increasingly…
body: There's no use in having a laptop that's powerful enough to do it all if it's not attached to a premium display. Why go to the effort of fine-tuning your game’s visual performance if you’re seeing the world through a sub-par monitor? How can you trust your videos look good to your viewers if they don’t look good to you? The Lenovo Legion 5i laptop's 15.3" WQXGA OLED display gives you plenty of space to spread out all your tasks, whether those involve gaming, homework, video editing, or all three at once.

The screen's snappy 165Hz refresh rate allows for smoother motion on-screen. Speed past screen tearing and lag with NVIDIA G-SYNC support, which syncs your monitor's refresh rate to your graphics card's frame rate for optimal performance. Watch movies in a brand-new light with the Lenovo Legion 5i’s DisplayHDR True Black 1000. And it's all on one laptop that doesn't compromise performance for its features.

articles.title: Struggling To Buy Magic’s Foundations Commander Decks? Wizards Confirms Reprints Are Likely
articles.summary: Magic’s new sets are great, but one of the most impressive (and surprising) products of the year has been the Foundations Commander decks. The five mono-colored preconstructed offerings have just started to sneak back down closer to MSRP, but with markups across the board and some (usually the…
body: Brandon Kreines, game producer on Magic: The Gathering at Wizards of the Coast, had good news for fans looking to grab each of the precons.
“The new Foundations Commander Decks are definitely intended to be an evergreen offering,” Kreines explained.
“We can’t commit to specifics, but if players are as excited about these decks as we are, they should expect to see them get reprinted so they can be used as an introduction point into Commander.”

That’s good news for just about everyone. After all, if you want to get into Commander, you’ll want to do it for MSRP where possible, and while some decks have been marked up to over double what they should cost, more printings will mean a drop in price.

articles.title: EA Just Shelved A Mysterious Sims Project—That Could Be Good News For Players
articles.summary: It's been another rough year for video games, with countless studio closures, staff layoffs, and projects that barely managed to even get off the ground before they were unceremoniously cut short.
body: This was especially painful for Mass Effect players, who were looking forward to the upcoming Mass Effect 5, which we now know was tentatively titled Mass Effect: Universe. But it's not just BioWare fans who are upset at the moment. Fans of EA's other properties are growing increasingly concerned about the future of those franchises, if any future is planned for them at all. My colleague Levi Winslow recently wrote about their concerns for the Skate franchise in the wake of layoffs at its development studio. Meanwhile, I'm quite worried about the fate of The Sims.

In the same breath it announced the end of BioWare, EA also reaffirmed its commitment to Apex Legends, Skate, and The Sims franchises. But everyone knows that when it comes to profits, EA's sports titles outrun its other IPs by a country mile. If EA is willing to pull the plug on legacy franchises like Mass Effect and Dragon Age, where does that leave its other franchises, like The Sims 4?
points: It's been another rough year for video games, with countless studio closures, staff layoffs, and projects that barely managed to even get off the ground before they were unceremoniously cut short.

"You’ll notice a special neck plate design celebrating Pokémon's 30th anniversary, too, commemorating the collaboration between Pokémon and Fender!"

Elsewhere in the Pokémon universe, the animated movie Pokémon: Wild Card was announced during the closing ceremony of the 2026 Pokémon World Championships, and it's due out in 2027. Meanwhile, Pokémon Pokopia was a huge hit for Nintendo Switch 2 this year, and we loved it. Finally, what about an R-rated Pokémon horror movie? One definitely hasn't been announced, but we'd love to see it.

articles.summary: The Australian Classification Board has rated Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, suggesting a port of Infinity Ward's original 2009 shooter may soon be revealed. The ACB updated its website to reflect a fresh R 18+ rating for the fan-favorite entry in the Activision franchise, with a classification…
body: The page, which is still live at the time of this piece's publication, specifically calls the title "Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2009)." As many others have already pointed out, the obvious assumption is that this is our first hint that a proper port will soon be revealed. Which platforms it may appear on was not shared, but fans may want to stay on their toes for an announcement.

There is one major reason to suspect Modern Warfare 2 (2009) may soon return: Activision tried the same strategy with the Black Ops series earlier this year. Ports for Black Ops 1 and 2 were leaked, announced, and launched all within the span of about one month back in June – and seemingly to much success. Black Ops 2, specifically, reportedly emerged as one of the best-selling games of the year in the month after its launch, but Activision's decision to replay its hits didn't arrive without controversy.

articles.title: CoD: Modern Warfare To Cut Real-Life Korean Tragedy Segment After Backlash
articles.summary: Publisher Activision has responded to criticism over using a devastating tragedy in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, saying that the incident will be removed from the military shooter in a November 12 update. The Seoul Halloween crowd crush occurred in October 2022 in Itaewon.
body: "Using such an incident as material for a game intended for entertainment purposes is itself highly inappropriate and a senseless act," the groups said, according to the BBC. "The Itaewon tragedy was a tragic disaster that produced hundreds of casualties, and citizens who participated in the rescue efforts or witnessed the event at the time continue to suffer from trauma. If the game developer has even a minimum level of courtesy and empathy toward the victims, they should promptly take corrective measures."

Activision has heard the call and plans to remove the depiction from Modern Warfare 4 when an update arrives on November 12. In responding to the criticism, Activision said it never intended to trivialize the disaster or make light of human suffering.

"In developing Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, we approached the subject matter with care and respect. The game’s opening cinematic utilises some real-world news coverage to establish the game’s fictional narrative," Activision said. "It is not intended to reference or trivialise the Itaewon disaster or any other real-world tragedy in any way, shape or form."
points: Publisher Activision has responded to criticism over using a devastating tragedy in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, saying that the incident will be removed from the military shooter in a November 12…

articles.title: New Assassin’s Creed Game Is Out Now, If You Don’t Mind Being Board
articles.summary: If you thought there wasn't going to be a new Assassin's Creed game this year, think again. It's not a video game, but Assassin's Creed: Animus is out today, turning the series into an adventure-style board game for 1-4 players.
body: A competitive game that pits players against each other as they explore distinct eras from the video games, Assassin's Creed: Animus features four protagonists to choose from in its standard edition: Eivor, Ezio, Altair, and Connor. The Collector's Edition, meanwhile, expands to 10 eras and features 16 protagonists, adding game characters like Edward Kenway, Jacob and Evie Frye, and Kassandra.

You and up to three of your friends (or you alone) work to complete objectives across these eras, taking down assassination targets in the way you see fit via "memory blocks." Whether you go in with your sword drawn or engage in a sneakier approach is up to you.

The standard version of Assassin's Creed: Animus is available to order now for $65, while the limited Collector's Edition costs $229. Alongside the extra characters and eras, this version comes with a storage box, acrylic tokens, a metal Piece of Eden, a cloth token bag, "special event cards," and an Animus Card Holder.
points: If you thought there wasn't going to be a new Assassin's Creed game this year, think again.

articles.title: 2026’s Secret 'Robin Hood' Movie Suddenly Drops on Streaming After Bombing in Theaters
articles.summary: Another 2026 box office flop is heading to streaming after a short theatrical run. The Uprising, which was briefly marketed in the U.S. as The Uprising: The Rise of Robin Hood, will stream exclusively on Peacock in early November.
body: While it’s become common for theatrical releases to hit streaming after just a few months, even the worst-performing films generally start with Video on Demand services like Prime Video and Apple TV, where rentals cost $20 or more. It seems The Uprising will be skipping this step entirely. The movie was released in U.S. theaters on Sept. 10, 2026, before grossing an unimpressive $8.2 million against a $20 million budget.

More pertinent to film fans, The Uprising received somewhat mixed reviews from critics and audiences alike. Only 57% of Rotten Tomatoes critics liked the picture, while 65% of Rotten Tomatoes user ratings were positive. While the film received praise for its performances, relevant social critique, and action, it was criticized for messy execution and a bland aesthetic. Those who didn't catch it in theaters can decide for themselves when the movie hits Peacock on Nov. 6.

articles.title: HBO’s New Green Lantern Series Officially Gets an Important Update
articles.summary: DC and HBO first announced My Adventures with Green Lantern back in 2025, and updates since then have been sparse. It was briefly shown off during this year's Annecy International Animation Festival, but nothing at the convention was released publicly.
body: Talking to Collider, Safran confirmed that the first season of My Adventures with Green Lantern will consist of 10 half-hour episodes. That matches the length of seasons of My Adventures with Superman, which the new show is a spun-off from. Safran added that while the themes of the Green Lantern show will be different than the Superman show due to the new roster of characters, it will be "tonally similar." That likely means it will mix traditional comic book action with some anime sensibilities.

While My Adventures with Green Lantern sounds like another exciting animated project for DC and HBO, it has a downside. The same team that makes My Adventures with Superman is leading work on the spin-off, meaning it may be a while before we see the likes of Clark, Louis, Jimmy, and Kara again. The show's third season was released earlier this year, but there has been no announcement of a fourth season yet. Safran told Collider that the future of the series is "up in the air right now."

articles.title: Sam Altman argues that it's bad you want DRAM in your computer and not a data center, actually
articles.summary: More and more, AI appears to be the reason we can't have nice things on the internet. Beyond generative models gobbling up my own and my fellow creatives' work in a bid to produce abysmally average output, AI data centres are also devouring all of the available memory.
body: Appearing on a recent episode of the Cheeky Pint podcast, Altman argued, "From a global allocation perspective, actually it’s quite terrible to have everyone have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer, and be used 5% of the time."

Yes, that is steam escaping from my ears. But before I go full screaming tea kettle, let's take a beat. For one thing, Altman is talking less about PC gamers specifically here, and more about solo AI bros craving compute power and "local inference".

To be clear, Altman is bemoaning an inefficiency within the AI industry rather than taking aim at us pesky gamers. He goes on to add, "You want maximum utilization in the cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply constrained environment. And somehow everyone's... Many people's intuition is the opposite of that."
points: More and more, AI appears to be the reason we can't have nice things on the internet.
Beyond generative models gobbling up my own and my fellow creatives' work in a bid to produce abysmally average output, AI data centres are also devouring all of the available memory.

articles.title: 6 Steam Games Coming Soon That Belong on Your Wishlist
articles.summary: Even though Steam Next Fest is over, we’re still sorting through all the games it put on our radar. While Steam’s recurring free demo event was invaded by generative AI games, it still featured plenty of human-made projects that cut through the slop.
body: To tie off the event, we combed through the most played demos during Steam Next Fest and pulled out the gems. Here are six games you’ll want to add to your wishlist, whether you’re a fan of co-op games, management sims, or volleyball.

Frostrail feels like a long-lost cousin of Frostpunk. The co-op shooter has you and your friends managing a steam-powered train as it barrels through a dangerous frozen wasteland. ( Train games are all the rage right now, it turns out.) You’ll have to scavenge for parts while fighting off horrifying monsters that lurk in the snow. It’s a perfect game for those upcoming winter months.

Abyssal Lapidary puts a very unique twist on the management sim genre. It puts you in charge of a gem shop, where you’re tasked with extracting minerals out of stone before turning them into precious jewelry. On top of that, the game has an eerie gothic setting that promises a layer of mystery.

articles.title: EA reportedly canned BioWare and Mass Effect 5 to make a new Star Wars: Battlefront instead
articles.summary: According to Bloomberg's sources, EA saw a new Battlefront game as a less risky investment than Mass Effect Universe. This final factor joined a host of well-discussed reasons for BioWare's unfortunate demise: Andromeda's critical reception, Anthem's live service failure, Veilguard's sales struggle…
body: One other added wrinkle: BioWare apparently lost its main ally at the top of the EA org chart. Entertainment and Central Development exec Laura Miele, who historically advocated for BioWare, was "sidelined" according to Bloomberg. EA sports execs David Tinson and Cam Weber were promoted instead. The age of nerds has ended, now begins the long night of the jock.

Overall, this new information doesn't radically reframe BioWare's overall story at EA, one of slow decline and mismanagement, or how most observers will interpret it through a culture war lens⁠. Was BioWare too woke? Not woke enough? For the love of god keep it out of our comments section. But now we know why the knife was finally driven home, for what it's worth.

And I guess we can anticipate a new Battlefront game some time at the tail end of the 2030s. Woohoo. For more on the closure of BioWare, PCG lead SEO editor Lauren Morton spoke to 16 developers who were inspired to join the industry because of the studio about what BioWare meant to them.
points: According to Bloomberg's sources, EA saw a new Battlefront game as a less risky investment than Mass Effect Universe.

articles.title: Which is scarier, Amnesia: The Dark Descent or Alien: Isolation? Vote now!
articles.summary: Presented by. This article is brought to you by No More Room in Hell 2. Last week, I asked PC Gamer readers to nominate the scariest PC games they could think of. I collected the top 16 submissions from that comment section (with some editorial discretion) and randomly seeded the bracket below.
body: After three rounds of voting, we're down to the final two games: Amnesia: The Dark Descent and Alien: Isolation.

To get here, Alien: Isolation beat SOMA, Darkwood, and Silent Hill 2, all by a decent margin. Amnesia: The Dark Decent was also a powerhouse, plowing through the acronym division—S.T.A.L.K.E.R. and F.E.A.R.—before facing off against one of its own, Amnesia: The Bunker. That was a closer race.

I know some of us at PCG consider The Bunker to be the scariest of the Amnesias, but the game that started it all is both more influential and a scary-ass game in its own right, and a strong competitor going into this final round.
Scroll down to cast your vote. Voting will be open until 9 am Pacific on Saturday, after which the winner will be crowned.

videos.summary: In this video, we dive deep into the complete Character Creation System for Hunter: The Reckoning - Deathwish! Whether you are a veteran of the World of Darkness or a tabletop RPG enthusiast looking for your next obsession, we've got you covered.
body: Watch as we walk you through every step of forging your ultimate Hunter:
- Appearance: Sculpting your unique look and physical identity.
- Attributes & Skills: Balancing your core stats to match your playstyle.
